summary: Over 150 Chinese apps block ByteDance's AI assistant from using them on a new phone, and Kim Jong Un crosses a new bridge into China.
body: China's big apps are pushing back against AI assistants that use other apps for you. More than 150 apps, including Tencent's WeChat and Alibaba's Alipay, have blocked ByteDance's Doubao assistant from operating them on Nubia's new "agentic" smartphone, the NaviX Ultra, Sixth Tone reports [^1]. The assistant works by reading the screen and tapping through apps after a spoken command, such as ordering food or booking a ride [^1]. Apps owned by Tencent and Alibaba make up nearly 60% of the blocked list, which also includes Meituan, Didi, Xiaohongshu, Pinduoduo, the three state telecom carriers, several banks and rival AI apps DeepSeek and Kimi [^1]. A Tsinghua University researcher told Cailian Press that China has no rules yet on how AI agents may operate other companies' apps, and that firms may be worried about privacy, data security and protecting their own AI products [^1]. My read: the same fight over who controls the user is coming to phones everywhere.

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un made his first trip to China in more than a year on Saturday, crossing the new 3-kilometre bridge over the Yalu River into the border city of Dandong [^2][^3]. He visited a memorial to China's role in the 1950-53 Korean War with senior Communist Party official Wang Huning, who passed on greetings from Xi Jinping, and toured a vehicle factory [^2][^3]. China finished its side of the bridge in 2014, but it only opened on Oct. 15 after years of strained ties; China's exports to North Korea reached a six-year high of $2.3 billion last year [^4]. AP notes Kim has spent recent years building ties with Russia, sending thousands of troops to help its war in Ukraine, and that Beijing is working to regain influence [^2].
